Went for a run to Sydney via the Hunter valley. Decided to see how she handled the dirt.

Went and had the bloody oil pressure sender wire fixed for teh 2nd time. My daisy chaining cable ties around the radiator hose and up to the frame to pull it off the wire proved to the dealer that it was a shorting issue. They re-routed the wire between the two radiator hoses so all is well.

This is probably just as well since my mates were getting too many opportunities to stir me up when I'd chuck another wobbly when the oil pressure ligth would flicker on.

ok it's actually quite simple.


Say your image is at www. photos. com / photo.jpg

all you need to do is wrap [img]and[/img] around it; e.g.

[img]www%20.%20photos%20.%20com%20/%20photo%20.%20jpg[/img]

simples!


what you posted above is HTML, which would work in a Pistonheads or eBay ad

Post 459 by LoSBoL, 02 Nov 2009, 06:37

#459
As far as I know there is only one sping kit for all the SD versions, standard and R... What makes the difference is the setup made by the specialist who installed the system.
The sping are the ones with the Hyperprogressive patented technolgy by Hyperpro and are full progressive, along the whole stroke.

Now the bike is softer on the road, you can feel more confidence when braking and leaning and when hitting bumps or holes wether you are on a straight or bent line... IMHO a huge improvement, far from the standard setup. The fork oil il SAE10 and the level is @ 140mm . Is also a good setup for track use if not seeking to squeeze the ultimate time lap. In that case compression and rebound shuld be tightened, while the preload not.
A side effect is that you can use the tyres with a higher pression also on the track, so that they are firmer, they last longer and better!

My better spent money as for the Motobox and the Akrapovic!!

Oh and I love my Duke!

bic_bicknell Forum member

Post 729 by bic_bicknell, 21 Mar 2010, 18:18

#729
So first day of spring and I finally get a 300+ mile ride. Package going really well with all the winter mods finished. Main ones are Motobox, PC111, SAS junked and shortened Akras converted to carbon sleeves.

Getting custom map on Tuesday so I will be very interested in seeing the first run because bike appears to be flawless fueling as is (on Akra map and whatever the PC111 came with a s base setting).

After getting used to the bike again on full throttle I think I need a shorter action throttle. And a steering damper - had a few 120mph shakes on bumpy A roads and the bike is definitely giving more torque as it goes front end light a lot more in second gear hard acceleration. I have resisted one up to now and followed the endless debates about them here but if you ride fast on UK roads I think you need one.

Or maybe it was just my enthusiasm.

Post 731 by bic_bicknell, 21 Mar 2010, 19:23

#731
That's right!

I live on a roundabout and I went straight away for the twisties and managed to find a route where I was leaned over the whole time! I don't think I ever went straight for more than 100 metres - and then I weaved about bit.

In my dreams.........

I'm watching that. It's cheap for a new damper and mounting kit. But then again it's a lot of money. I've also been searching for a Scotts damper and they make this look cheap!! I have to find a way to explain it to Amy - but she was in Southhampton this weekend and went clothes shopping. So when she gets back I need to find out how much she spent because maybe, just maybe, I could justify this. Best way is to explain that it makes riding a bit less of a risk with one fitted. It's a safety feature isn't it? Like a dayglo belt really. If I say that the police recommend them......

Post 793 by Millar, 02 Apr 2010, 09:35

#793
The R-seat is not uncomfortable, it's just hard. There's a distinct difference. It's very wide, so it doesn't feel like you're flossing your butt-hole. There's no problems with moving around on it. The only real complaint I have about it is that it's quite slippery. Solutions to that is sticky leathers and/or to put some sticky residue on the seat. Or stomp-grips.

And keep in mind, it's "", not "Custom", not "GT", not "Gold Wing".... R..!! R!! It's not supposed to be "comfortable".
So if you're an "All show - No Go" there's your punishment already.

Post 907 by emuexport, 13 May 2010, 08:53

#907
This is me after waiting 3 hrs for a pick-up after being stranded approximately in the middle of bumf*k nowhere. No cell phone reception, not much traffic. One of the guys I was riding with had to ride half hr back up the rd to get reception and organise the pick-up.
Luckily, it was a nice day and I had another riding companion to keep me company.
The guy turns up with the trailer and pulls a six pack out of the car "I bet you guys are thirsty!" damn straight.
Done the starter motor torque limiter.. we had stopped to wait for a friend who wasn't that far behind, admirable effort for a 600, and she just didn't start again, lots of clacking and bad noises. Tried to bump start several times with no luck, what a bitch that was.
Anyway, she is in the shop now and I expect to have it back in the garage soon.
Wouldn't give her up for anything.

Post 1343 by cdlabate, 17 Jan 2011, 08:03

#1343
I finally got a good group ride in on the Superduke today. The weather was most excellent here in Santa Cruz Cali! On my bike was the newly installed Motohooligan box with the secondary flies, sas removal, and crash bungs. I also tested the CRG Arrow mirror. I was quite impressed with the mirror, lots of visibility and stable. It's true what they tell you about the motohooligan box! It certainly does smooth out the throttle. Bike felt way different going into and exiting corners and is much more tolerable at slow pace city riding. The Motohooligan Box is by far the best mod I have done to my bike. I'm still running the stock cans and haven’t remapped yet, but there is definitely a noticeable improvement.

I'm painting my headlight bucket. While i was at it couldn't help but move things around . I would love to mount the guages right where they are in this photo -


I've also thought about doing the headlight bucket swap thing but next photo i'd like to keep the KTM windscreen but it would be mounted just a bit higher than stock as in photo. Just a simple bracket to make if loosing the headlight bucket.

the only issue i've had with all the aftermarket headlight stuff is can't find one that keeps the transparent windscreen - and i like the KTM one.... If i loose the Bucket would be really easy to mount a light there . The other easy step would be to make a cover the for wiring box that's all behind the stock headlight. And finally doing this would take moving the ignition switch to the spot right in front of the ECU and mount it sideways in there ( enough wiring already there to do so )....

Anyway just my thoughts for now. Gona paint bucket and put back stock for now.
some guys Cringe at the thought of modifying a perfectly good stock bike - i don't LOL

KTM666 Forum member

Post 1588 by KTM666, 25 Aug 2011, 00:22

#1588
So just got back from about 70 miles round trip rippin it ..... Cord showing last 4 rides - yup mistake i know ... Was at 120mph uphill today on this rear tyre - the cord lengthened itself by about 8 inches - was only half that size before this latest romp...

I tried to do as KTM GUY suggests and wear the sides out before the middle , but i just have a hard time staying off the throttle on this bike. slightly over 2 months ago i bought this tyre and said "i'm going to go easy on the straights" so i can wear the sides first ---- Well that sure didn't happen.... i think i got about 3,000 miles out of it though ... I like the tyre - Dunlop Q2's the new ones. And the deal on them lately 200 bucks for a set is hard to pass up , and i've never had the tyres give while hard cornering ,

Really getting used to reverse shifting , My unasked for advice to anyone going to put the reverse shift kit on is -DO NOT try racing around through twisties etc until you're sure yu have all the reflexes , and mistake proof nerve patterns before you start ripping ... I ride quite a bit of serious twisties and today was my 7th outing on reverse shifting .. I"m just about up to speed.

have fun



i forgot to mention - i encourage any of you eager eaters ( like i am ) to loose the weight - i have lost about 10 lbs from 200 to 190 on my 5'8" whole inches of body and i tell you the bike's acceleration is getting quicker , i'm gona shoot for another 10 lbs and get down to 180 lbs....

Bike really seems to be enjoying it (-:

That's coz the front pressure is right and the rear is too low mate.

They're not the same as motorsport handmade N Techs.

Hot pressures of Sportsmarts on an SD 32 front 30 rear. Will grip ok and won't tear up.

Just of top of my head without checking my notes I'm sure cold pressures are usually 4psi lower.


Bit of topic like

Just for comparison...
Those Interacts I sent, the rear had very slight cold tear. It only took 2psi more pressure to get it running clean.

There's how the new ones look running just 2psi more. Don't even look like they've been on track.

Post 1977 by dade, 30 Dec 2012, 22:14

#1977
In Italy if the value of the bike is less than the damage the insurance pays you the Eurotax value, so you can buy yourself a similar used bike, like the old beloved you couldn't repair. Then you have to destroy the bike in an authorised center (i.e: you give to the center the frame, the plate and the certificate of ownership and so the bike officially isn't existent any more). Then again with all the stuff you've streaked from your ex-bike you fund the purchase of a used bike like yours or a new one. So I have to choose between a 2008 SD, a SD-R 132 or (hopefully) an Aprila Tuono V4... who knows... The only problem is the big loss of time... two months have been passed and i wonder how many other will, before I'll get my money from the French insurance...

Hope to have a bike for the two days KTM Test'N'Track in Mugello Circuit at the end of March...

Winter projects done ? Hey ! Winter just started, but I have been busy. Got the solo kit mounted on an orange painted sub frame. Waiting on some CF fenders and heal guards from Adam. E-mailed him yesterday and he has 7 pieces to do before he gets to mine. Got a steering dampner installed, WP mounted down under, KTM tank protector for the jacket zippers....
Got another project going on my KTM 950 Adventure. Making a rear lugage / crash bar. Got a 7/8 tube fastened from the buddy peg , bent and wrapped all the way around the back to the tail light and back to the other buddy peg. It's supported from the tail luggage pad by 3/8 tube, welded up and painted last night. I cad'ed up a new tail rack Monday. Need to make some chips. I will make some side panels from aluminium sheet that spans between the rack and the crash bars. Then I will make 4 dry bags 24 inches x 7 inch diameter to strap to the sides snuggly. The top rack tail bag will be expandable up to 14 inches tall, but will live at 7 tall when not carrying...supplies to the camp site

I will have to say I really enjoied Pauls build...little to fussy for the likes of me. I end up using my tools to the max. It sure was fun to follow his build and really set the hook in me to become addicted to this KTM site. Thanks Paul !
Keep on wrenchin', winter will end before you know it

My 650 XRR goes over 100. OSSA Yankee That was rare as hens teeth. A 2 smooker V twin You must be a old fart too I got my first ride on a modern dirt bike back in 1972 on a new OSSA Pantom ?. I had a HD Super 10 at the time. My brother inlaw let me ride his new bike and I did what you do on a dirt bike..hauled ass. I got back and I was really jassed. Wow !
It had brakes, suspension and power. Then he chew my ass for riding it the way I did. Fookin pissed me off, and never asked him for anything again. He does have the bragging rights of beating Malcom Smith.
My brother and his brother in law rode enduos. There was a sound check at the start. They would fasten tyre intubes to thier tail pipes long e-nuf to drag on the ground to quite the bikes down. When the got out of sight of the marshels they woud run over the other guys intertube with thier front wheels which would pull the tubes off for more power.

Got my cast off and kwires removed last week, so whilst I still have a messed up left hand I couldn't resist and took the new SD, (new to me) out for a run. Removed the original mirrors and put on a new set of barend mirrors that arrived yesterday.

Now, it can't be just me, but does anyone else just turn into a nutter when they get on one of these??? I couldn't help myself, popping wheelies out of intersections (it actually makes me look good at them ) Every hump in the road I would give it a blip and up it would come. I jumped it off a lip in the road in town like a dirtbike It is so damn easy to ride like a big dirtbike. I threw it into some corners and I swear I could pick the front end up whilst changing direction. The only thing I would like for it is a steering damper as it felt a bit squiggly at times.

HYPERMOTO Forum member

Post 2473 by HYPERMOTO, 22 Jun 2015, 10:50

#2473
I think it's really loud. Having akras on my 990 with the db killers removed, it feels to me this is a lot louder than that. It may have something to do with where the exhaust exits when sitting on the bike. Only a proper meter would tell. I need to get hold of one. I've tried both the 35mm and 50mm insert and the difference seems marginal, but the 35mm is smoother at low revs.

I haven't got the map yet but it's on the agenda to be done in the next few weeks.

There may be an issue at full lean as it sits as far out as the pegs do, and obviously lower too, but I don't think it would be a problem for me any time soon.

Short video after putting the 50mm insert in. Was early in the morning and didn't want to piss the neighbours off so nothing at full throttle. I'll do another one soon.
